summary: In this September 22 video, the Couch Investor seriously considers selling AMD after it crossed a $1 trillion market cap and $600/share (up ~176% year-to-date), having bought since ~$80-110 when others called it 'catching a falling knife.' He recaps the Meta strategic partnership — 160M shares at a penny if AMD hits $600 plus ~6GW of GPU deployments, with milestones still to be hit — and market expectations: ~47% revenue growth this fiscal year, ~73% next (to ~$88B on Helios), ~38% in FY28 (~$121.3B), with data center now 58% of revenue and a 60%+ long-term segment growth target. His DCF: base case roughly at fair value (about 1% expensive), bull case ~$1,150, bear case 58.1% lower, probability-weighted $685 (~12-13% upside) — some figures garbled in auto-captions. His core argument: at ~55x forward earnings and ~113x forward free cash flow, holding a trillion-dollar AMD requires growth beyond what's baked in, and the market now demands AMD justify a huge premium over Nvidia, which trades at 18.8x forward earnings with faster expected growth and a $5.4T cap. He leans toward taking profits and reallocating to Nvidia and/or Broadcom — or keeping cash for fintech names if the rate environment improves — while stressing he isn't hating AMD and will notify portfolio followers the moment he moves, with a fuller update in the Sunday portfolio video. Calls per supplied list: AMD SELL (profit-taking under consideration); AMD HOLD @ ~$600 (currently held).
title: I Might Sell AMD Stock. Here's Why

calls.thesis: Shareholder since ~$100; DCF base case says ~1% overvalued at $600, prob-weighted target $685 (~12% upside); trending toward taking profits and rotating into NVDA/AVGO/MU/META or cash.
calls.bull_case: Bull DCF: $1,150 (+80.6%) on faster growth + 38%+ EBIT margins.
